summary: Derm Foundation is a machine learning model designed to accelerate AI development for skin image analysis for dermatology applications using pre-trained embeddings. It produces a 6144-dimensional embedding vector as output.
keywords: machine learning; dermatology; image analysis; embeddings; skin conditions
intended_use_and_workflow: Derm Foundation can reduce the training data, compute, and technical expertise necessary to develop task-specific models for skin image analysis. Embeddings can be used for classifying clinical conditions, scoring severity, identifying the body part, and determining image quality.
primary_intended_users: Businesses and institutions in healthcare and life sciences, researchers.
how_to_use: Use example code snippets to get started running the model locally. For use at scale, create a production version using Model Garden. The model can be loaded directly from Hugging Face Hub.
model_limitations: Derm Foundation's quality can degrade in extreme lighting or noise conditions. It was trained on data from a limited set of countries and settings, so it may not generalize well to other data. The model only generates embeddings and does not generate any predictions or diagnoses.
outcomes_and_output: The model produces a 6144-dimensional embedding vector as output, which can be used for downstream tasks.
type_and_value_of_solution_output: Embedding vector of floating point values (Dimensions: 6144)
explanation_for_how_an_output_is_generat: Derm Foundation is pre-trained on large amounts of labeled skin images to produce 6144 dimensional embeddings that capture dense features relevant for analyzing these images.
input_data_source: A large number of health-related image-text pairs from the public web and tele-dermatology datasets from the United States and Colombia, a skin cancer dataset from Australia, and additional public images.
output_input_data_type: Input: PNG image file 448 x 448 pixels. Output: Embedding vector of floating point values (Dimensions: 6144)
development_data_characterization: The Derm Foundation model utilizes a BiT ResNet-101x3 architecture and was trained in two stages. The first stage involved contrastive learning on a large number of public image-text pairs. The second stage fine-tuned the image component for condition classification using clinical datasets.
training_data: The model was trained in two stages: pre-training and supervised fine-tuning (SFT). The pre-training stage used a large number of health-related image-text pairs from the public web. The SFT model used tele-dermatology datasets from the United States and Colombia, a skin cancer dataset from Australia, and additional public images.
demographic_representativeness: The supervised fine-tuned (SFT) model was trained using data from a limited set of countries (United States, Colombia, Australia, public images) and settings (mostly clinical). It may not generalize well to data from other countries, patient populations, or image types not used in training. [SOURCE 1]
relevance_of_training_data_to_intended_p: The SFT model was trained on data from a limited set of countries (United States, Colombia, Australia, public images) and settings (mostly clinical), which may impact its generalization to other countries, patient populations, or image types not used in training. [SOURCE 1]
usefulness_efficacy_goal_of_metrics: Derm Foundation was evaluated for data-efficient accuracy across a range of skin-related classifications tasks [SOURCE 1].
usefulness_efficacy_result: Training a linear classifier on Derm-Foundations embeddings were substantially more performant (10-15% increase in accuracy) than doing the same for a standard BiT-M model across different proportions of training data [SOURCE 1].
usefulness_efficacy_interpretation: Models built on top of the Derm Foundation embeddings for dermatology-related tasks achieved significantly higher quality than those built solely on embeddings or fine tuned from BiT-M; this advantage was most pronounced for smaller training dataset sizes [SOURCE 4].
usefulness_efficacy_test_type: The model's performance was tested by training models on a downstream task using teledermatology data, using varying dataset sizes (12.5%, 25%, 50%, 100%) to compare embedding-based linear classifiers against fine-tuning [SOURCE 4].
usefulness_efficacy_testing_data_descrip: The SFT (supervised fine-tuned) model was trained data from a limited set of countries (United States, Colombia, Australia, public images) and settings (mostly clinical) [SOURCE 1].
usefulness_efficacy_validation_process_a: Downstream models built using Derm Foundation still require careful evaluation to understand their expected performance in the intended setting [SOURCE 4].
